walkthroughs.body_html:
Formulae & Equations — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Formulae & Equations brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Formulae & Equations.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The formula of magnesium chloride is:
options: MgCl₂
MgCl
Mg₂Cl
MgCl₃

mcqs.q: Which is the correctly balanced equation for magnesium burning in oxygen?
options: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO
Mg + O₂ → MgO
Mg + O₂ → MgO₂
2Mg + 2O₂ → 2MgO

mcqs.q: The state symbol for a substance dissolved in water is:
options: (aq)

mcqs.q: How many oxygen atoms are in one formula unit of Ca(NO₃)₂?
Does the state symbol (l) mean dissolved in water?
options: No — (l) means a pure liquid such as molten or liquid substances; dissolved substances are shown as (aq).
(l) means the substance is a gas kept at low temperature.
(l) stands for 'in liquid', so it means the substance is dissolved in water.
You balance equations by deleting products you do not want.

mcqs.q: Can you change the small subscript numbers in formulae to balance an equation?
options: Writing MgO₂ instead of MgO is an acceptable way to balance the oxygen atoms.
No — subscripts define the identity of each compound; you balance only by writing numbers in front of whole formulae.
The 2 means there are two calcium atoms.
You balance equations by deleting products you do not want.

mcqs.q: In Ca(NO₃)₂, does the 2 outside the bracket multiply only the oxygen?
options: No — it multiplies everything inside the bracket, giving two nitrogen atoms and six oxygen atoms.
The 2 means there are two calcium atoms.
(l) means the substance is a gas kept at low temperature.
The 2 applies only to the last atom written, the oxygen.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Valency”?
options: An equation showing only the ions and atoms that actually change in a reaction; spectator ions are left out.
Numbers placed in front of formulae make the count of each type of atom equal on both sides of the equation.
The combining power of an atom or ion, used to work out formulae by balancing positive and negative charges.
(s), (l), (g) and (aq) show whether each substance is a solid, a liquid, a gas, or dissolved in water.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Balancing equations”?
options: Numbers placed in front of formulae make the count of each type of atom equal on both sides of the equation.
The combining power of an atom or ion, used to work out formulae by balancing positive and negative charges.
Shows the type and number of each atom in a substance; H₂O contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
(s), (l), (g) and (aq) show whether each substance is a solid, a liquid, a gas, or dissolved in water.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ionic equation”?
options: (s), (l), (g) and (aq) show whether each substance is a solid, a liquid, a gas, or dissolved in water.
Numbers placed in front of formulae make the count of each type of atom equal on both sides of the equation.
Shows the type and number of each atom in a substance; H₂O contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
An equation showing only the ions and atoms that actually change in a reaction; spectator ions are left out.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “State symbols”?
options: Atoms are neither created nor destroyed in a reaction, so the total mass of products equals the total mass of reactants.
Numbers placed in front of formulae make the count of each type of atom equal on both sides of the equation.
Shows the type and number of each atom in a substance; H₂O contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
(s), (l), (g) and (aq) show whether each substance is a solid, a liquid, a gas, or dissolved in water.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Chemical formula”?
options: Atoms are neither created nor destroyed in a reaction, so the total mass of products equals the total mass of reactants.
An equation showing only the ions and atoms that actually change in a reaction; spectator ions are left out.
Shows the type and number of each atom in a substance; H₂O contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
The combining power of an atom or ion, used to work out formulae by balancing positive and negative charges.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Conservation of mass”?
options: An equation showing only the ions and atoms that actually change in a reaction; spectator ions are left out.
The combining power of an atom or ion, used to work out formulae by balancing positive and negative charges.
Atoms are neither created nor destroyed in a reaction, so the total mass of products equals the total mass of reactants.
Numbers placed in front of formulae make the count of each type of atom equal on both sides of the equation.

mcqs.q: How many atoms in total are in one molecule of sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄?
options: 7 atoms
5 atoms
4 atoms
6 atoms
